entities.summary: Eurybiades was the Spartan navarch in charge of the Greek navy during the Second Persian invasion of Greece, played a key role in the Battle of Salamis, and successfully defended the Greek fleet against the invading forces of King Xerxes I. His leadership and strategic decisions were instrumental in the Greek victory, which marked a significant turning point in the Persian Wars. The Battle of Salamis was a crucial moment in Greek history, as it thwarted the Persian attempts to conquer Greece and paved the way for the eventual defeat of the Persians at the Battle of Plataea. Eurybiades' actions also had a lasting impact on the development of the Greek navy, which became a powerful force in the Mediterranean. The Battle of Salamis is still studied by historians and naval strategists today, and Eurybiades' name has become synonymous with bravery and military genius. As the last of the Spartan navarchs, Eurybiades' legacy extended beyond his own lifetime, influencing the course of Greek history and shaping the destiny of the city-state of Sparta. In the centuries that followed, Eurybiades' name would be invoked by historians and politicians alike, serving as a symbol of Spartan pride and defiance in the face of overwhelming odds.
